```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Setup"
library(opal)
library(ggplot2)

data(io_yft_data)
data(io_yft_parameters)
data(io_yft_map)
data(io_yft_reference)

ref   <- io_yft_reference
d     <- io_yft_data
n_ts  <- d$n_year
truth <- ref$truth$trajectory
ss3   <- ref$ss3$trajectory

# Model outputs precomputed by data-raw/generate-io-yft-vignette-cache.R, so
# the article renders without rebuilding the RTMB model
cache <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "io_yft_vignette_cache.rds", package = "opal"))
c2    <- cache$models$C2

fmt <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
options(knitr.kable.NA = "—")
fleet_name <- function(f) sprintf("%d: %s", as.integer(f), ref$fleet_names[as.integer(f)])
last <- function(df, v) df[[v]][df$ts == max(df$ts)]

series_col <- c("opal C2" = "#1E8449", "SS3" = "grey20", "Simulated truth" = "#D4AC0D")
scale_series <- list(scale_colour_manual(values = series_col, name = NULL))
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
            theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))
```

This vignette fits opal to a simulated Indian Ocean yellowfin tuna data set
and compares the result with the Stock Synthesis 3 (SS3) model built for the
same data, and with the simulated truth those data came from. Everything it
needs is bundled with the package: the opal inputs, a stored fit, and
summary tables from SS3 and from the operating model.

# Background

## The data and the SS3 model

The data are replicate 4 of the Indian Ocean yellowfin operating model (OM)
of the
[Spatial Stock Assessment Simulation Experiment](https://aaronmberger-nwfsc.github.io/Spatial-Assessment-Modeling-Workshop/articles/OM_description_YFT.html).
The OM was built in the Spatial Population Model software (SPM; Dunn,
Rasmussen and Mormede 2015) and conditioned on Indian Ocean Tuna Commission
(IOTC) fishery data (Dunn, Hoyle and Datta 2020). It is spatially explicit:

* **Space and time.** The population lives on a 5° × 5° grid of 159 ocean
  cells, in quarterly time steps from 1952 to 2015 (256 quarters), with ages
  1–28 quarters (28 is a plus group).
* **Recruitment.** One stock with one Beverton–Holt stock–recruitment
  relationship (steepness 0.8) on the total spawning biomass. Quarterly
  recruitment strength varies (lognormal, SD 0.6), and each quarter's
  recruits are spread across cells by a spatial apportionment layer with its
  own random variation.
* **Movement.** Fish move between cells every quarter according to habitat
  preferences for sea surface temperature, chlorophyll-a and distance,
  separately for immature and mature fish. Maturation moves fish from the
  immature to the mature state.
* **Fishing.** Seven gear-type fisheries remove their observed catches
  exactly, cell by cell, using exploitation rates.
* **Data.** Catch (without error), longline CPUE, length frequencies and tag
  recaptures are simulated cell by cell.

For the experiment, the simulated data were aggregated to the four regions of
the IOTC yellowfin assessment and to a single area. Because the data are
simulated, the true spawning biomass and unfished spawning biomass (B0) are
known. The truth files report them by assessment region; here they are summed
over the whole domain. Spawning biomass is mature biomass at the start of the
quarter, before fishing, in tonnes, the same definition as SS3's.

The SS3 model (SS3 v`r ref$ss3$version`) is the IATTC analyst team's
single-region estimation model for that experiment, built by Mark N.
Maunder, Haikun Xu and Carolina Minte-Vera. It treats each quarter as a
model "year", so it runs `r n_ts` time steps. opal takes the same time steps
(`n_year = ` `r n_ts`, `n_season = 1`) and SS3's ages 1–`r d$n_age`, so the
opal age index equals the SS3 age. Although the SS3 model is
single-region, it keeps the four-region structure in its fleets: its 16
extraction fisheries are gear × region combinations from the four-region
data (for example, `fishing_ll_1` to `fishing_ll_4` are longline in regions
1–4). SS3's mean length-at-age is the OM's own (Fu et al. 2018, after Fonteneau and Gascuel 2008), so growth is
known exactly.

```{r}
#| label: dimensions
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  quantity = c("Time steps (quarters)", "Ages", "Extraction fisheries",
               "Index series (longline CPUE, one per quarter)",
               "Fisheries with length compositions", "Length bins"),
  value = c(n_ts, d$n_age, 16, 4, length(d$lf_fishery_f), d$n_len)),
  col.names = c("Quantity", "Value"))
```

Catch is in numbers. The longline CPUE index is split into four quarterly
series, each with its own catchability (opal fisheries 17–20). Length
compositions enter as multinomials, with SS3's variance adjustments
(`mult_by_lencomp_N`) carried across.

## Converting SS3 to opal

The opal inputs were produced by an SS3-to-opal converter
([wcpfc-bet-single-region](`r ref$source$repository`), `code/rtmb`). It reads
the SS3 data, control, parameter and report files, and its output reconciles
exactly with SS3 for catch, the index, the length compositions and biology
(M, weight, maturity and spawning potential at age). Fitted at SS3's own
parameter values, opal tracks SS3's spawning biomass to within 10%, and that
gap comes entirely from when catch is removed within the quarter (see
[Model differences](#model-differences)).

The first conversion used opal's single-k Schnute growth curve. SS3 uses its
`GrowthModel 3`, where K changes with age, and the Schnute curve cannot
follow it: it was 5–16 cm too long at ages 4–8. Through the length
compositions, that shifted the fitted stock size well away from SS3's. opal
now implements SS3's age-specific K growth as an option to `get_growth()`
(`log_k_mult` and `k_mult_ages`), and the bundled inputs use it with SS3's
growth parameters.

```{r}
#| label: growth
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Mean length-at-age at the start of the quarter: SS3, opal with SS3's age-specific K (as used here), and the single-k Schnute curve used in the first conversion."
p <- io_yft_parameters
laa_opal <- get_growth(d$n_age, d$A1, d$A2, exp(p$log_L1), exp(p$log_L2), p$log_k,
                       min_age = d$min_age, log_k_mult = p$log_k_mult,
                       k_mult_ages = d$k_mult_ages,
                       plus_group_adjust = isTRUE(d$growth_plus_group_adjust))
growth_lab <- c("SS3", "opal, SS3 age-specific K", "opal, Schnute (first conversion)")
growth <- rbind(
  data.frame(ref$ss3$length_at_age, series = growth_lab[1]),
  data.frame(age = d$age_a, length = laa_opal, series = growth_lab[2]),
  data.frame(ref$schnute_length_at_age, series = growth_lab[3]))
growth$series <- factor(growth$series, growth_lab)
# SS3 is drawn wide underneath so the identical opal curve stays visible.
ggplot(growth, aes(age, length, colour = series, linetype = series, linewidth = series)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c("grey70", "#1E8449", "#C0392B"), growth_lab),
                      name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = setNames(c("solid", "dashed", "dotted"), growth_lab),
                        name = NULL) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = setNames(c(2.2, 0.8, 0.8), growth_lab), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Age (quarters)", y = "Mean length (cm)")
```

With growth matched (largest difference
`r fmt(max(abs(laa_opal - ref$ss3$length_at_age$length)), 4)` cm), the
remaining differences between the two models are structural. The table
below follows the fits from the first conversion to the one in this
vignette. The first two hold selectivity at SS3's estimates; C2 estimates
opal's own.

```{r}
#| label: history
h <- ref$history
knitr::kable(data.frame(h$model, B0_ratio = h$B0 / ref$ss3$ssb0, h$terminal_depletion),
             digits = c(0, 2, 3),
             col.names = c("opal fit", "B0 / SS3 B0", "Terminal SSB / B0"))
```

SS3's terminal SSB / B0 is `r fmt(last(ss3, "static_dep"), 3)`.

## Model differences

opal and SS3 are both age-structured, but they make different structural
choices. The ones that matter for this model are:

| | SS3 (this model) | opal |
|---|---|---|
| Growth | `GrowthModel 3`, age-specific K | The same, through `get_growth()` with `log_k_mult` |
| Timing of biology within the quarter | Catch, length compositions and the index use mid-season length-at-age and abundance | Everything is evaluated at the start of the quarter |
| Catch | Hybrid F (`F_Method = 3`): F and M act together through the quarter (Baranov) | The quarter's catch is removed at the start, then M acts |
| Selectivity | Age-based: double normal (fisheries), logistic (survey) | Length-based double normal and logistic, mapped to age through the probability of length at age |
| Spawner-recruit timing | Age-0 recruits at *t* from SSB at *t* | Age-1 recruits at *t* + 1 from SSB at *t* + 1 (SS3's age 0 is not carried) |
| Index | One series, one analytic catchability | Four quarterly series, four estimated catchabilities |
| Survey size-frequency data | Generalised size compositions (λ = 0.51) | Not included |
| Equilibrium plus group | Iterated to 3 × the number of ages | Closed-form geometric tail (≈5e-5 difference in SPR0) |
| Priors | None on ln R0 or selectivity | N(0, 2) on selectivity parameters; weak normal priors on log B0 and log q |

Catch timing is the largest. At SS3's own parameter values it alone moves
opal's spawning biomass by up to 10%, because under heavy catch opal ends
each quarter with more fish than the Baranov equation leaves.

# The assessment

The bundled inputs start at SS3's solution: SS3's unfished spawning biomass,
recruitment deviations and recruitment bias ramp. Growth, natural mortality,
steepness and σ_R are fixed at SS3's values. Selectivity curves start from
opal curves fitted to SS3's selectivity, projected onto length.

```{r}
#| label: build
assessment <- opal_obj(
  data = io_yft_data,
  parameters = io_yft_parameters,
  map = io_yft_map,
  control = list(eval.max = 10000, iter.max = 10000),
  metadata = list(stock = "Indian Ocean yellowfin (simulated)", model = "C2")
)
```

## Selectivity

The map estimates the opal equivalents of the selectivity parameters SS3
estimated.

```{r}
#| label: sel-map
sel_free <- matrix(!is.na(io_yft_map$par_sel), nrow = nrow(io_yft_parameters$par_sel))
sel_level <- matrix(as.integer(io_yft_map$par_sel), nrow = nrow(io_yft_parameters$par_sel))
own <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(sel_level)), function(f) {
  lv <- sel_level[f, !is.na(sel_level[f, ])]
  if (!length(lv)) return("none (fixed)")
  src <- which(apply(sel_level, 1, function(r) any(r %in% lv)))[1]
  if (src != f) sprintf("mirrors fishery %d", src) else
    paste(which(sel_free[f, ]), collapse = ", ")
}, character(1))
family <- c("logistic", "double normal", "double Richards")[d$sel_type_f]
knitr::kable(data.frame(fishery = fleet_name(seq_along(own)), family = family,
                        estimated = own),
             col.names = c("Fishery", "opal curve", "Estimated parameter columns"))
```

For the double normal, columns 1–4 are the peak, plateau, ascending width
and descending width, the same order as SS3's pattern 20 parameters P1–P4.
Columns 5 and 6 (initial and final selectivity) were fixed in SS3 and stay
at their starting values here.

Nine parameters SS3 estimated are fixed in this configuration. Estimated
freely, they settle at the mean of opal's N(0, 2) selectivity prior: the
length data do not inform them. They are the plateau and descending width of
the asymptotic fisheries 4, 5, 7 and 13, where selectivity reaches 1 before
the largest lengths observed, and fishery 9's descending width. Fixing them
at their starting values gives the same fit (likelihood components agree to
the third decimal), without the result depending on the prior.

## Fit

Fitting takes a few minutes, so the vignette uses the stored result. The
fit below was made from exactly these inputs.

```{r}
#| label: fit
#| eval: false
fit <- opal_fit(assessment, n_passes = 2L)
```

The stored fit also polishes the optimum with Newton steps and runs
`opal_check()` with a gradient tolerance of 1e-4
(`data-raw/generate-io-yft-c2-fit.R`).

The stored fit is `inst/extdata/io_yft_c2_fit.rds`. Reading it and
rebuilding the model for `opal_report()` takes about a minute, so the
figures below use outputs precomputed from it
(`data-raw/generate-io-yft-vignette-cache.R`):

```{r}
#| label: load-fit
#| eval: false
fit <- opal_read(system.file("extdata", "io_yft_c2_fit.rds", package = "opal"))
summary(fit)
report <- opal_report(fit)
```

```{r}
#| label: fit-summary
cat(c2$fit$summary, sep = "\n")
B0 <- c2$B0
```

```{r}
#| label: fit-check
v <- c2$fit
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  quantity = c("Estimated parameters", "Objective", "Max |gradient|", "opal_check()"),
  value = c(v$n_par, fmt(v$objective, 3),
            formatC(v$max_gradient, format = "e", digits = 1),
            if (isTRUE(v$passes)) "passed" else "failed")),
  col.names = c("Quantity", "Value"))
```

# Fits to the data

## Index

```{r}
#| label: index-fits
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Observed longline index (points, ±1.96 SE) with opal's predictions and SS3's expected values. Each quarterly series is on a mean-one scale."
cp <- d$cpue_data
idx <- data.frame(ts = cp$ts, fishery = cp$fishery, obs = cp$value, se = cp$se,
                  pred = c2$cpue$pred)
pred <- rbind(data.frame(ts = idx$ts, fishery = idx$fishery, value = idx$pred, series = "opal C2"),
              data.frame(ts = ref$ss3$cpue$ts, fishery = ref$ss3$cpue$fishery,
                         value = ref$ss3$cpue$expected, series = "SS3"))
ggplot() +
  geom_linerange(data = idx, aes(ts, ymin = obs * exp(-1.96 * se), ymax = obs * exp(1.96 * se)),
                 colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(data = idx, aes(ts, obs), size = 1, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line(data = pred, aes(ts, value, colour = series), linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ fishery, ncol = 1, labeller = as_labeller(fleet_name)) +
  scale_series +
  labs(x = "Time step (quarter)", y = "Index (mean = 1 per series)")
```

```{r}
#| label: index-rmse
rmse <- function(o, p) sqrt(mean((log(o) - log(p))^2))
knitr::kable(data.frame(model = c("opal C2", "SS3"),
                        rmse = c(rmse(idx$obs, idx$pred),
                                 rmse(ref$ss3$cpue$obs, ref$ss3$cpue$expected))),
             digits = 4, col.names = c("Model", "RMSE of log residuals"))
```

## Length compositions

```{r}
#| label: comp-aggregate
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Length compositions aggregated over all observations for each fishery, weighted by sample size: observed (bars), opal's predictions and SS3's expected values."
agg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(d$lf_fishery_f), function(j) {
  obs  <- d$lf_obs_data$obs[[j]]
  obs  <- obs / rowSums(obs)
  n    <- d$lf_n_fi[[j]]
  data.frame(fishery = d$lf_fishery_f[j], bin = d$len_lower,
             observed  = colSums(obs * n) / sum(n))
}))
agg <- merge(agg, c2$lf, by = c("fishery", "bin"))
ss3_lf <- ref$ss3$lf
lines <- rbind(data.frame(fishery = agg$fishery, bin = agg$bin, value = agg$predicted,
                          series = "opal C2"),
               data.frame(fishery = ss3_lf$fishery, bin = ss3_lf$bin, value = ss3_lf$expected,
                          series = "SS3"))
width <- diff(d$len_lower[1:2])
ggplot() +
  geom_col(data = agg, aes(bin + width / 2, observed), fill = "grey80", width = width) +
  geom_line(data = lines, aes(bin + width / 2, value, colour = series), linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ fishery, ncol = 4, scales = "free_y", labeller = as_labeller(fleet_name)) +
  scale_series +
  labs(x = "Length (cm)", y = "Proportion")
```

With the growth curves identical, opal's predicted compositions differ from
SS3's through selectivity and the within-quarter timing.

# Selectivity

```{r}
#| label: sel-age
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Selectivity-at-age: SS3 (age-based) and opal C2 (length-based, mapped to age)."
sa <- rbind(
  data.frame(c2$sel_age, series = "opal C2"),
  data.frame(ref$ss3$sel_age, series = "SS3"))
ggplot(sa[sa$fishery <= 17, ], aes(age, sel, colour = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ fishery, ncol = 4, labeller = as_labeller(fleet_name)) +
  scale_series +
  labs(x = "Age (quarters)", y = "Selectivity")
```

Fisheries 15 and 16 mirror 14, and panel 17 stands for all four quarterly
index series. opal's curves are functions of length and reach age through
the spread of length at age, so they rise more gradually than SS3's
age-based curves. Several dome-shaped curves (fisheries 2, 3, 6, 8, 11 and
12) fall faster after the peak in opal but level off above zero at the
oldest ages, where SS3's fall towards zero. The largest difference is
fishery 5, where opal's ascending limb is much shallower, and its fit to
that fishery's length compositions is closer to the data.

# Stock status

```{r}
#| label: trajectories
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Spawning biomass (top) and static depletion SSB / B0 (bottom): opal C2, SS3 and the simulated truth."
traj <- rbind(
  data.frame(c2$trajectory, series = "opal C2"),
  data.frame(ss3, series = "SS3"),
  data.frame(truth, series = "Simulated truth"))
traj$series <- factor(traj$series, names(series_col))
long <- rbind(data.frame(ts = traj$ts, series = traj$series, value = traj$ssb / 1e6,
                         panel = "Spawning biomass (million t)"),
              data.frame(ts = traj$ts, series = traj$series, value = traj$static_dep,
                         panel = "SSB / B0"))
ggplot(long, aes(ts, value, colour = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  scale_series +
  labs(x = "Time step (quarter)", y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: recruitment
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Recruitment deviations, opal C2 against SS3. opal's deviation for time step t sets the age-1 recruits entering at t + 1."
rd <- merge(data.frame(ts = seq_along(c2$rdev), opal = c2$rdev),
            ref$ss3$recdevs, by = "ts")
ggplot(rd, aes(recdev, opal)) +
  geom_abline(colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6, colour = series_col[["opal C2"]]) +
  labs(x = "SS3 recruitment deviation", y = "opal recruitment deviation")
```

```{r}
#| label: comparison-table
compare <- function(x, y) {
  m <- merge(x, y, by = "ts")
  c(mean_pct = mean(abs(100 * (m$ssb.x / m$ssb.y - 1))),
    max_dep_err = max(abs(m$static_dep.x - m$static_dep.y)))
}
opal_traj <- traj[traj$series == "opal C2", c("ts", "ssb", "static_dep")]
vs_ss3   <- compare(opal_traj, ss3)
vs_truth <- rbind(compare(opal_traj, truth), compare(ss3, truth))
tab <- data.frame(
  model = c("opal C2", "SS3", "Simulated truth"),
  B0 = c(B0, ref$ss3$ssb0, ref$truth$b0) / 1e6,
  B0_truth = c(B0, ref$ss3$ssb0, ref$truth$b0) / ref$truth$b0,
  vs_ss3 = c(vs_ss3[["mean_pct"]], NA, NA),
  vs_truth = c(vs_truth[, "mean_pct"], NA),
  terminal = c(last(opal_traj, "static_dep"), last(ss3, "static_dep"), last(truth, "static_dep")),
  dep_err = c(vs_truth[, "max_dep_err"], NA))
knitr::kable(tab, digits = c(0, 2, 2, 1, 1, 3, 3),
             col.names = c("Model", "B0 (million t)", "B0 / true B0",
                           "SSB mean |% diff| from SS3", "SSB mean |% diff| from truth",
                           "Terminal SSB / B0", "Max |depletion error| vs truth"))
```

# Summary

* With SS3's growth, opal's length-at-age matches SS3's, and the bundled fit
  converges and passes `opal_check()`.
* opal C2's B0 is `r fmt(B0 / ref$ss3$ssb0, 2)` × SS3's and its terminal
  depletion is `r fmt(last(opal_traj, "static_dep"), 3)`, against SS3's
  `r fmt(last(ss3, "static_dep"), 3)` and a true
  `r fmt(last(truth, "static_dep"), 3)`.
* Held at SS3's selectivity, opal reproduces SS3's stock size closely
  (B0 `r fmt(ref$history$B0[2] / ref$ss3$ssb0, 2)` × SS3's). C2's lower
  stock size comes from the selectivity curves opal estimates from the
  length compositions. Its depletion trajectory nonetheless follows
  SS3's closely for most of the series and drops below it late on.
  Estimating SS3's own age-based curves instead gives a similar stock size
  (`vignette("io-yft-age-selectivity", package = "opal")`), so the
  difference is not that opal's curves are length-based.
* Neither model is the truth. SS3 overestimates B0 by
  `r fmt(100 * (ref$ss3$ssb0 / ref$truth$b0 - 1), 0)`%; the operating model
  has movement among 159 cells and spatially varying recruitment, which
  neither single-region model represents. Matching SS3 and matching the truth are separate questions.

# Credit and references

The SS3 model was developed by the IATTC analyst team (Mark N. Maunder,
Haikun Xu and Carolina Minte-Vera, Inter-American Tropical Tuna Commission)
for the Spatial Stock Assessment Simulation Experiment. The yellowfin
assessments from the experiment, including theirs, are evaluated in:

* Goethel, D.R., et al. (2024). 'Drivin' with your eyes closed': Results from
  an international, blinded simulation experiment to evaluate spatial stock
  assessments. *Fish and Fisheries* 25(3): 471–490.
  <https://doi.org/10.1111/faf.12819>

The age-specific K growth model is Stock Synthesis' `GrowthModel 3`:

* Methot, R.D. Jr., and Wetzel, C.R. (2013). Stock synthesis: A biological
  and statistical framework for fish stock assessment and fishery
  management. *Fisheries Research* 142: 86–99.
  <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fishres.2012.10.012>

The data and the simulated truth are from replicate 4 of the Indian Ocean
yellowfin operating model
(<https://github.com/aaronmberger-nwfsc/Spatial-Assessment-Modeling-Workshop>):

* Dunn, A., Rasmussen, S. and Mormede, S. (2015). Spatial Population Model.
  NIWA Technical Report 138.
* Dunn, A., Hoyle, S.D. and Datta, S. (2020). Development of spatially
  explicit operating models for yellowfin tuna populations in the Indian
  Ocean. IOTC Working Party on Tropical Tunas 22.
* Fu, D., Merino, G., Langley, A. and Ijurco, A. (2018). Preliminary Indian
  Ocean yellowfin tuna stock assessment 1950–2017 (Stock Synthesis). IOTC
  20th Working Party on Tropical Tunas.
* Fonteneau, A. and Gascuel, D. (2008). Growth rates and apparent growth
  curves, for yellowfin, skipjack and bigeye tagged and recovered in the
  Indian Ocean during the IOTTP. IOTC-2008-WPTDA-08.

The SS3-to-opal converter and the detailed conversion vignettes are in
<`r ref$source$repository`> (`code/rtmb`); the bundled data were exported by
`r ref$source$script` at commit `r ref$source$commit`. The opal outputs shown were computed with
opal `r cache$opal` (commit `r cache$commit`). Age-based selectivity, which
SS3 uses here, is compared with C2 in
`vignette("io-yft-age-selectivity", package = "opal")`.
